newsitem.title: USA: U.N. says no Iraqi oil deal contracts pending.
newsitem.headline: U.N. says no Iraqi oil deal contracts pending.

text.p: U.N. overseers have no contracts from prospective buyers of Iraqi oil pending review, leaving the tally for approved contracts under the oil-for-food deal at five, according to a U.N. spokesman Friday.
"They have none pending," said the spokesman, noting the situation had not changed from late Thursday.
Since the start of the $2 billion oil for food plan, U.N. overseers have received and approved five contracts.

Turkish state oil company TUPRAS received permission to buy 75,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Iraqi oil on Tuesday. An additional four contracts were okayed Thursday, including contracts believed to be from U.S.-firm Coastal Corp and France's Elf Aquitaine.

Under the renewable oil deal, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of crude over a six month period in order to buy food and aid for civilians, suffering from sanctions imposed on Iraq after it invaded Kuwait in August, 1990.
